_meta.introduced_in: v10.497 governance batch, Stage B Wave 1
consumed_by: CANONICAL_TRUTH_REGISTRY.md (every domain has a classification field)
doctrine: G1 — Every governed artifact has exactly one classification state
G2 — Classifications express intent and lifecycle, not quality
G3 — Transitions are events, not gradients
G4 — Enforcement severity is independent of classification
G5 — `unknown` is a temporary state, never a destination

canonical.meaning: This artifact IS the source of truth for its domain; alternatives are violations
invariants: Has at least one enforcement gate

derived.meaning: Computed view, projection, or cache of one or more canonical sources; no independent authority
invariants: Has derived_from declaration pointing at canonical sources
Can be rebuilt from sources at any time without info loss

transitional.meaning: Exists today, used today, being actively replaced/refactored/harmonized; rules temporarily relaxed
invariants: Enforcement gates apply at reduced severity (HIGH/MEDIUM, not CRITICAL) during window
examples: v1 admin endpoints with confirm: bool = False instead of require_admin

deprecated.meaning: Existed, served a purpose, no longer source of truth; may exist for legacy/audit but not for writes
deprecated.notes: Cannot return to canonical without explicit unretirement (constitutional event)

unknown.meaning: Discovered but role/classification/authority not yet determined; survey state only
invariants: Cannot remain unknown longer than 1 batch

canonical_with_transitional_subareas.meaning: Parent canonical; one or more sub-fields/sub-functions in transitional state

transitional_subareas: v1 admin endpoint RBAC (confirm: bool = False instead of require_admin)

transitional_toward_canonical.meaning: Transitional, target is canonical (most common compound)

transitional_toward_deprecated.meaning: Transitional because being retired; use until retirement actually completes

canonical.derived: rare — canonical becomes derived if rebuilt as computed view

all_valid_transitions_require: Audit gate adjustment (severity, scope, or both)
Entry in REVIVAL_LEDGER.md with date and rationale

CRITICAL.meaning: Compromises system integrity, security, or canonical truth
CRITICAL.behavior: fail immediately; blocks certification; aborts CI/CD
examples: Password not bcrypt-hashed on new account
Canonical role string used outside role_taxonomy resolution path

HIGH.meaning: Should not exist long-term; may be permitted during declared harmonization window
HIGH.behavior: during grace window — passed with warning; after deadline — behaves as CRITICAL
examples: transitional artifact violating target contract after deadline
new code path bypassing existing canonical interface

MEDIUM.meaning: Drift, technical debt, or governance gap; tolerable during current harmonization phase
MEDIUM.behavior: reported in audit summary; flagged for owner; does not block certification
examples: Documentation inconsistency between code and .md artifact
Test coverage in single module below per-module target but above floor
transitional past 50% grace window with no progress
Stale backup files past retention policy

LOW.meaning: Finding worth visibility — drift candidates, optimization, style — no integrity impact
LOW.behavior: listed in audit report under advisories; does not block
examples: unknown artifacts past target wave but non-blocking

phase_1_visibility.behavior: Gate runs; violations reported at LOW regardless of inherent severity; no blocking

phase_2_grace.behavior: Severity escalates to inherent default; owners must remediate or document exception; blocking only at CRITICAL

phase_3_full_enforcement.behavior: Severity final; CRITICAL and HIGH block; no more soft transitions

permanent_exemptions.mechanism: # noqa: <gate_name> in code OR registry-level exemption

open_items_for_subsequent_waves: All Wave 5 specialty domains need canonical-interface contracts surveyed to confirm canonical status
